backlog.spec: Replace the standard Adam optimizer updates with Bayesian Adam (BayesAdam) which uses a global, learnable approximation to the second moment, potentially improving convergence on unstructured text data without architecture changes.
backlog.title: Bayesian Adam Optimizer

backlog.spec: Combine a linear warmup phase with a standard cosine decay schedule rather than pure linear interpolation, often providing steeper initial gradients that help early learning.
backlog.title: Cosine with Linear Warmup

backlog.spec: Switch standard Transformer layers to use LayerNorm instead of BatchNorm, which has been shown to improve generalization and reduce vanishing gradients in sequence modeling tasks.
backlog.title: Batch Norm with LayerNorm Hybrid

backlog.spec: Replace standard LayerNorm with Layernorm-M (from PyTorch 2.5+) which uses a multi-scale expansion of input to compute statistics, often improving stability.
backlog.title: Multi-利的 Layer Norm

backlog.spec: Substitute standard self-attention with spatial attention mechanisms that process sequences spatially, potentially capturing local dependencies better.
backlog.title: Spatial Attention

backlog.spec: Use a state-space model (SSM) based architecture (like Mamba) instead of Transformer, which offers linear complexity in sequence length and high efficiency.
backlog.title: Foundational Inference

backlog.spec: Replace the random initialization standard implementation with Deep Fourier Mixtures for attention, potentially improving generalization.
backlog.title: Deep FM

backlog.spec: Enable gradient checkpointing (re-computation) during the forward pass to reduce memory usage by half, allowing for larger effective batch sizes or faster training without VRAM constraints.
backlog.title: Gradient Checkpointing

backlog.spec: Lower the training precision from fp32 to fp16 or bf16 where possible, or use AMP (Automatic Mixed Precision) techniques to accelerate training.
backlog.title: AMP Precision

backlog.spec: Train with variable batch sizes per example using a dynamic scheduler that fits the entire batch into the sequence if possible, improving efficiency.
backlog.title: Adaptive Per Token Batch Size

backlog.spec: Add small dropout (0.1) to the Adam regularization term to improve robustness against overfitting.
backlog.title: AdamW Dropout

backlog.spec: Increase the number of gradient accumulation steps to effectively simulate a larger per-step batch size, allowing the model to learn from more data per update.
backlog.title: Gradient Accumulation

backlog.spec: Apply layer-wise adaptive filter for dense vectors (init), potentially improving initialization of deep layers.
backlog.title: Layer-wise AFED

backlog.spec: Apply a robust scaling to gradients (like vanilla gradient norm scaling but robustified) to handle outliers better.
backlog.title: Robust Local Gradient

backlog.spec: Use Nevet weight decay (a variant of L2 regularization) that is more adaptive to the structure of the weights.
backlog.title: Nevet Weight Decay

backlog.spec: Apply quantization to the LayerNorm weights and bias terms to reduce memory footprint and improve throughput on A100.
backlog.title: Quantized LayerNorm

backlog.spec: Replace standard attention with Soft Attention (softmax over attention scores) which is smoother and more differentiable.
backlog.title: Soft Attention

backlog.spec: Apply cross-entropy smoothing to the target distribution during training, which reduces overfitting on rare tokens.
backlog.title: Cross-Entropy Smoothing

backlog.spec: Add batch-level bias terms to the attention mechanism, improving the model's ability to adapt to different data batches.
backlog.title: Batch Level Bias

backlog.spec: Replace standard L2Norm with L2Norm plus alpha (a variant that adds alpha to the L2Norm), improving generalization.
backlog.title: Scheduled Dropout

backlog.spec: Apply a masked feed-forward network with a quadratic activation function, which is more expressive and requires less data.
backlog.title: Masked FFN

backlog.spec: Use a global norm fusion technique that combines information across the entire batch, improving scaling.
backlog.title: Global Norm Fusion

backlog.spec: Apply LayerNorm specifically to the output of each layer, improving stability.
backlog.title: Layer-Specific LayerNorm

backlog.spec: Apply LayerNorm to the cross-attention mechanism, improving cross-attention performance.
backlog.title: Cross-Attention LayerNorm

backlog.spec: Replace BatchNorm with FusedBatchNorm which is more efficient and can be implemented in fused operations.
backlog.title: Fused BatchNorm

backlog.spec: Apply adaptive layer normalization where the weights and biases are learned per layer but shared across the batch, improving generalization.
backlog.title: Adaptive LayerNorm

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmup with a cosine warmup followed by a cosine decay, potentially improving convergence.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Schedulers

backlog.spec: Apply gradient clipping with a norm-based scaling factor that adapts to the current batch's gradient magnitude, improving stability.
backlog.title: Gradient Clip Coverage

backlog.spec: Ensure that batch normalization is applied consistently across all layers and inputs, preventing instability.
backlog.title: Batch Normalization Stability

backlog.spec: Use AdamW with a gamma parameter that scales the weight decay, improving generalization.
backlog.title: AdamW with Gamma

backlog.spec: Replace the Adam optimizer with the Grady optimizer, which uses second-order moments and can compute gradients approximately without storing Hessian matrices, reducing memory overhead and speeding up convergence on small batches.
backlog.title: Grady Optimizer

backlog.spec: Replace the current linear warmup and cosine decay schedule with a three-phase schedule: linear warmup for 10% of the budget, constant high LR for 40%, then cosine decay for 50%. This extension reduces the dead zone in training and improves generalization on short training sequences.
backlog.title: Three-Phase Learning Rate Scheduler

backlog.spec: Replace the linear projection layer at the input of the transformer block (before the attention or MLP) with a linearized version that outputs a vector whose dimension is equal to the sequence length, simplifying the network and reducing overfitting on small datasets.
backlog.title: Linearized Output Projection

backlog.spec: Reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 16 and increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE via gradient accumulation to 32, to ensure more optimizer steps per batch and stronger regularization, while keeping the total tokens per second constant.
backlog.title: Count-Skip Batch Size

backlog.spec: Apply a layer-wise gradient filter that zeros out the gradient of each layer if the sum of squares of the weight gradients is below a threshold (e.g., 0.001), to prevent unstable updates in unconverged layers.
backlog.title: Layer-wise Gradient Filtering

backlog.spec: Replace the ReLU activation in the feed-forward network with a parametric activation that learns a weight matrix W such that ReLU(x + W * 1), where 1 is a vector of ones, to dynamically control the activation range along all dimensions.
backlog.title: Parametric FFN Activation

backlog.spec: After the first 50% of the training budget, adapt the learning rate for each layer by setting it to the reciprocal of the mean absolute value of the gradient vector of that layer's parameters during the current step, to accelerate convergence on hard layers.
backlog.title: Adaptive Learning Rate per Layer

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed sliding window pattern with a dynamic window mask that is determined by the maximum gradient magnitude in the current batch, expanding the context window to 2x if the gradient magnitude is large and shrinking it otherwise.
backlog.title: Dynamic Window Mask

backlog.spec: Drop the optimizer and instead perform a gradient descent step using the gradient of the loss function with respect to the parameters, scaled by the reciprocal of the mean gradient magnitude, to simulate a more robust update.
backlog.title: Gradient-based Gradient Descent

backlog.spec: Replace the raw gradient accumulation step with a varying-precision accumulation schedule, using fp16 accumulation for early steps to reduce variance and switch to fp32 accumulation for final micro-steps to stabilize gradients without losing flow continuity.
backlog.title: Mixed Precision Accumulation Scheduling

backlog.spec: Replace the scalar alpha used in the attention layers learning a per-head alpha parameter instead, allowing each attention head to adaptively adjust its scaling factor based on its own activation scale.
backlog.title: Per-Head Adaptive Alpha for Affine attention

backlog.spec: Introduce a stochastic hiddle layer dropout schedule that increases the fraction of dropped layers as training progresses, focusing on higher layers first to allow early layers to specialize and then gradually destabilize deeper representations.
backlog.title: Curriculum Multi-cale Stochastic Depth

backlog.spec: Replace the standard linear attention kernel with a frequency-aware attention kernel that separately attends to low-frequency and high-frequency components of the input sequence using a two-stage attention mechanism.
backlog.title: Frequency-Aware Transformer Architecture

backlog.spec: Apply a batch-specific gradient weighting method that applies a different weighting function to gradients based on the batch's global norm, allowing higher-noise batches to receive more conservative updates.
backlog.title: Batch-Specific Gradient Weighting

backlog.spec: Replace the global learning rate schedule with a self-aware learning rate scheduler that adjusts the learning rate based on the variance of the gradients themselves, allowing the model to self-regulate its learning speed.
backlog.title: Self-Aware Learning Rate Adaptation

backlog.spec: Replace the static sliding window mask with a dynamic window mask that changes the window size and stride based on the layer's current learning rate and gradient norms, allowing the model to adaptively reduce or increase context support over time.
backlog.title: Dynamic Window Mask with Layerwise Scales

backlog.spec: Introduce an EMA momentum parameter for the batch norm layers that updates the batch norm statistics at a slower rate than the input statistics, stabilizing the batch norm statistics over time.
backlog.title: Batch Normalization with EMA Momentum

backlog.spec: Replace the global gradient clipping with a layer-wise gradient filtering method that selectively clips the gradients of specific layers based on their current significance, allowing important layers to update normally while stabilizing less important ones.
backlog.title: Layer-wise Gradient Filtering

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed warmdown schedule with a gradient-sensitive warmdown schedule that adjusts the learning rate based on the current gradient magnitude, allowing the model to warmdown faster when gradients are small and slow when gradients are large.
backlog.title: Schedule with Gradient-Sensitive Warmdown

backlog.spec: Replace the global FINAL_LR_FRAC and WARMDOWN_RATIO with a schedule that computes a per-layer learning rate multiplier based on the layer's depth (e.g., linearly increasing from 0.8 to 1.2 across the stack) applied to the base LR.
backlog.title: Per-Layer Learning Rate Scaling

backlog.spec: Introduce a sub-step normalization where gradients are clipped not just to a global norm but also to the median gradient norm per micro-step, then re-normalized globally to prevent occasional spikes from dominating updates.
backlog.title: Gradient Magnitude Clipping with Substep Normalization

backlog.spec: Modify the existing stochastic depth (if present) or add a drop-path mechanism that down-weights deeper layers by a factor proportional to frequency importance (e.g., 1/exp(depth * 0.1)) to focus learning on shallow features.
backlog.title: Stochastic Depth Re-weighting by Frequency

backlog.spec: Replace the static RMSNorm epsilon with a learnable scalar per layer that converges to a small positive value during training, effectively tuning the normalization stability on the fly.
backlog.title: Adaptive RMSNorm Epsilon

backlog.spec: Before softmax, apply a small clip-val operation to the K matrix so that values exceeding the mean + a small sigma (e.g., 2*std) are clamped, reducing attention to extreme outliers and stabilizing gradients.
backlog.title: Attention Masked Predecessor Clipping

backlog.spec: Instead of decaying LR globally at the end of the epoch, apply an exponential decay to the LR multiplier every N micro-steps (e.g., 10 steps) during the warmdown phase, smoothing the effective learning rate curve.
backlog.title: Micro-Step Learning Rate Decay

backlog.spec: Add a learnable gate to the value projection path: V = gate * (V_proj + V_residual) where V_residual is a small fraction of the previous layer's output, allowing selective retention of past context.
backlog.title: Value Projection with Gated Residuals

backlog.spec: Maintain a short window of past gradients per micro-step. Before the weight update, compute a weighted average of current and historical gradients and use that averaged gradient for the update step.
backlog.title: Gradient History Accumulation

backlog.spec: Randomly shuffle the order of tokens within each micro-step window at the start of every micro-step but restore their original order before softmax, breaking spatial autocorrelation without losing information.
backlog.title: Window Size Permutation

backlog.spec: Divide the residual stream into groups (e.g., every 4 layers) and apply a separate alpha parameter to the residual connection strength for each group, allowing the model to learn optimal skip patterns dynamically.
backlog.title: Residual Grouping with Layer-wise Alpha

memo:
Incumbent mean_adjusted is 1.1146 over 16 runs. Nothing tried has clearly beaten it. Three single runs landed slightly below it: gradient-norm clipping at 1.0 (1.1122), previous-token key mixing (1.1127) and the gradient-norm EMA scale (1.1131). These gaps are small and each is one run, so they may be noise.

What hurt: cutting optimizer steps (TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**20, +0.0704), checkpointing with a larger device batch (+0.0419), schedule reshaping (cosine +0.0205, three-phase +0.0143), and extra regularization (layer dropout +0.0151, label smoothing +0.0040). The gated MLP also hurt (+0.0088).

Next: replicate clipping first, then combine it with key mixing. After that, try a smaller TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE for more steps, then tune the learning rate and warmdown ratio, then depth/width trade-offs. Read train.py before proposing ideas. Many slots were wasted on no-edit ideas it already covers.
